privacy.heroLead: PulseFlow is a digital health platform connecting patients and healthcare professionals. Here we explain how we process personal and health data transparently, in line with Brazil’s LGPD.
privacy.s1p1: PulseFlow treats privacy and security as priorities. This policy describes what we collect, why we use it, who may access it, and your rights, in accordance with Law No. 13.709/2018 (LGPD) and applicable health and professional secrecy rules.
privacy.s2intro: Depending on your role (patient or professional) and how you use the platform, we may process:
privacy.s2li1: Registration data: name, email, phone, CPF when required or provided, date of birth, and professional credentials (e.g. medical license and state) for doctors.
privacy.s2li2: Health data entered in the platform: medical record, clinical events (e.g. blood pressure, diabetes, symptoms), exam attachments, visit notes and information provided by you or your physician.
privacy.s2li3: Usage and technical data: access logs, IP address, browser type, device identifiers and cookies needed for session operation and security.
privacy.s2li4: Optional integration data: information from wearables or devices when you authorize sync with PulseFlow.
privacy.s3li1: Deliver the services: registration, authentication (including two-step verification when enabled), scheduling, notifications and record management.
privacy.s3li2: Allow authorized professionals to access information needed for care, respecting platform permissions and relationships.
privacy.s3li3: Comply with legal and regulatory obligations, respond to competent authorities and exercise rights in legal or administrative proceedings.
privacy.s3li4: Improve stability, security and user experience (using aggregated metrics where possible).
privacy.s3li5: Send important notices about your account, the platform or changes to this policy.
privacy.s4intro: We apply technical and organizational measures appropriate to the risk, including:
privacy.s4li1: Encrypting communications with HTTPS (TLS) between your device and our services.
privacy.s4li2: Access controls, strong authentication where available and logical segregation of data.
privacy.s4li4: Periodic security reviews aligned with LGPD and good practices for sensitive health data.
privacy.s4box: Health data is processed with heightened confidentiality and only for the purposes described or permitted by law.
privacy.s5li1: Confirm whether we process your data and access it.
privacy.s5li2: Correct incomplete, inaccurate or outdated data.
privacy.s5li3: Request anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary data or data processed unlawfully.
privacy.s5li4: Withdraw consent when processing is consent-based, subject to legal limits.
privacy.s5li5: Request portability to another provider, where applicable.
privacy.s5li6: Obtain information on sharing and, where applicable, object to irregular processing.
privacy.s6p1: We do not sell your data. We may share information only when necessary to operate the platform (e.g. cloud hosting under confidentiality agreements), with authorized professionals in a care context, or with third parties to comply with law or court orders.
privacy.s7p1: To exercise your rights or ask questions about this policy, email pulseflowsaude@gmail.com. We will respond within the timelines and procedures required by LGPD.

terms.heroLead: General conditions for using PulseFlow by patients and healthcare professionals.
terms.s1p1: By accessing or using PulseFlow (website, logged-in areas and related features), you confirm that you have read and agree to these Terms and the Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, do not use the platform.
terms.s1p2: We may update these Terms; the last update date appears on the legal pages. Continued use after material changes means you acknowledge the new terms, except where the law requires specific consent.
terms.s2intro: PulseFlow provides digital tools for health information management, communication between patients and professionals, scheduling and clinical follow-up, according to the features available at each time. You must not:
terms.s2li1: Use the platform for unlawful, fraudulent or non-health-related purposes outside the intended use.
terms.s2li2: Attempt to access accounts, data or restricted areas without authorization.
terms.s2li3: Introduce malware, perform attacks or abusive scraping that harms stability or security.
terms.s2li4: Unauthorized copying of software, brands or PulseFlow content.
terms.s3li1: Keeping your password and additional authentication factors confidential.
terms.s3li2: All activity under your account until you notify us of misuse.
terms.s3li3: Providing truthful information and keeping it up to date.
terms.s3li4: Promptly reporting suspicious access or lost devices with active sessions.
terms.s3box: Secure account use is essential to protect health data. Use strong passwords and never share credentials.
terms.s4p1: PulseFlow — including software, interface, text, trademarks and documentation — is protected by intellectual property laws. You receive only a limited, revocable, non-transferable licence to use the platform under these Terms.
terms.s5intro: PulseFlow is a support tool for health information management. Nothing on the platform replaces professional assessment, diagnosis or clinical decisions. In particular:
terms.s5li1: We are not liable for medical decisions based solely on platform data without professional judgment.
terms.s5li2: Temporary outages may occur; we use reasonable efforts for availability and security without guaranteeing uninterrupted operation.
terms.s5li3: To the fullest extent permitted by law, we limit liability to direct damages caused by a serious platform failure, excluding lost profits and indirect damages unless otherwise required by law.
terms.s6p1: We may modify, suspend or discontinue features for maintenance, improvement or legal reasons. When reasonable, we will notify you of material changes through the platform.

security.heroLead: How PulseFlow protects clinical information and personal data across the digital journey.
security.card1Text: Traffic between your browser/app and our services is protected with HTTPS (TLS), reducing interception risk.
security.card2Text: Where available, two-step verification and password policies strengthen access for professional accounts.
security.card3Text: Role-based permissions (patient, physician, admin) so each user sees only what their role requires.
security.card4Text: Backup routines and recovery plans to reduce data loss in incidents.
security.card5Text: Infrastructure and security event monitoring to detect anomalies and abuse.
security.card6Text: Audit logs for relevant platform actions, supporting compliance and internal review.
security.s1p1: PulseFlow was designed knowing how sensitive health data is. We work under LGPD, professional secrecy and security good practices for health systems.
security.s1p2: This page summarizes measures in general terms; operational details may evolve while our commitment to protection remains.
security.s2li1: TLS encryption for all communication with APIs and web interfaces.
security.s2li2: Server hardening, network segmentation where applicable and security patching.
security.s2li3: Protection against unauthorized access and password policies.
security.s2li4: Periodic security testing proportional to risk.
security.s2li5: Logical separation of data between tenants or contexts, per environment architecture.
security.s3intro: Sensitive health data receives heightened protection:
security.s3li1: Access only by authorized professionals and accounts, according to care relationships and settings.
security.s3li2: Logs that support tracing relevant access and changes when the feature is available.
security.s3li3: Respect for the Medical Code of Ethics and CFM rules applicable to computerized systems.
security.s3li4: Confidentiality by default, except on legal grounds, consent or treatment necessity.
security.s3li5: Data subject rights under LGPD and the Privacy Policy.
security.boxHtml: Important: Professionals must keep credentials confidential. Misuse may lead to ethical, civil and criminal consequences.
security.s4p1: If an incident may significantly affect data subjects, we will take containment and notification measures under LGPD and ANPD guidance.
security.s4contactHtml: To report vulnerabilities or suspicious activity: pulseflowsaude@gmail.com.
security.s5intro: LGPD rights include confirmation of processing, access, correction, anonymization, portability, information on sharing and withdrawal of consent where applicable. See also our Privacy Policy.
security.s6p1: This page may be updated to reflect security improvements or legal changes. Please review it periodically.
security.s6p2Html: More on data processing: Privacy Policy.

faq.heroLead: Answers about PulseFlow: access, medical record, exams, security and roles for doctors and patients.
faq.q1: How does a physician sign in?
faq.a1: Professionals sign in on the web with email and password. When two-factor authentication (2FA) is enabled, you must enter a one-time code sent by email (or another configured method) after your password. This helps protect patient data.
faq.q2: How do I find a patient?
faq.a2: In the clinical workspace, search by CPF (and other available filters) to open the patient profile linked to your care. From there you access the record, clinical events, attachments and reports allowed by the platform.
faq.q3: What can I see in the record?
faq.a3: Depending on what the patient logged and what was documented in visits, you may see events such as blood pressure, diabetes, migraine, gastritis crises, menstrual cycle, among others, plus attached exams, notes and care history.
faq.a4: Patients can upload files (e.g. PDF or images) linked to the record. You view and download them according to system permissions, with a history organized for clinical review.
faq.a5: The platform may show charts and trends from longitudinal records (e.g. blood pressure or glucose). They support clinical reading but do not replace professional assessment.
faq.a6: An extra step after your password: a short-lived code sent to email (or another configured method). It reduces unauthorized access even if the password is leaked.
faq.a7: Patients can enter information in the patient area (web or available flows); physicians document during care. Updates appear according to synchronization and permission rules.
faq.q8: What is the difference between the physician and patient areas?
faq.a8: The physician area focuses on patient search, record, scheduling and clinical tools. The patient area supports self-care and sharing data with the care team. Both are part of the same PulseFlow ecosystem.
faq.moreHtml: Write to pulseflowsaude@gmail.com. We will be glad to help.
